context: A police officer briefs a manager about traffic enforcement
purpose: Teach: 支障/通行/務める/打ち出し/最善/適度/応える/相次い

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 通行規制、御社の物流に支障を来していますね。
lines.en: The road closures are creating real pressure on your logistics operations.
lines.style: Measured, professional opening. Direct eye contact. Calm authority without coldness. Acknowledging the burden as genuine, not dismissive. Steady pace.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。安全を最優先で務めるという方針で動いています。
lines.en: Yes. We're operating under a safety-first policy across the board.
lines.style: Respectful but grounded. Not obsequious — speaking from a position of competence. Small pause before the affirmation, gathering himself. Clear, deliberate emphasis on 'safety first.'

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 迂回案、相次いで打ち出しを進めていますが、適度な選択を。
lines.en: We're rolling out detour options continuously. Choose the ones that actually work for you.
lines.style: Practical, slightly matter-of-fact. A hint of permission underneath — he's giving Kenji agency, not just directives. Steady, efficient pacing. Professional warmth at the edges.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 住民の声に応える形で、最善策を選びます。
lines.en: We'll choose the best option — one that actually listens to what the residents need.
lines.style: Quiet commitment. No performance. Weight settling on the words 'residents' and 'best.' Slower pace here — this is sincere, not procedural. Steady gaze.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.en: The department will work with you on this.
lines.style: Firm but not cold. A small nod of reassurance — moving from procedural to partnership. Warm undertone. Slightly softer attack than the first line, but still measured.
